digests.title: AI 日报｜11月28日：多维模型评估与 Agent 落地瓶颈
digests.summary: 本期关注模型多维评估、Agent 集成与流程改造难题，以及 datasette-charts 0.4a0 的插件扩展改进。[S3][S6][S13]
digests.content:
## 今日重点

### 模型评估：从总榜排名转向能力画像

一组帖子提出，模型评分应更像 RPG 的多属性面板，而不是单一排行榜。作者以让 Claude、Codex 为同一条推文生成图片为例：他认为 Claude 的结果更美观、思考更充分，而 Codex 更贴近自己的原始意图，并据此呼吁开发相应评测。[S3][S4][S5]

**编辑判断：**这一例子提示，视觉质量、创造性与意图遵循可能需要分开衡量；但现有材料只是作者的个案主观评价，不能据此判定两款工具的整体能力高低。[S4]

### Agent 落地：系统集成之外，还要重做工作流程

Aaron Levie 认为，个人和组织可能满足于最初带来惊喜的 AI 用法，尚未充分探索后台 Agent 或处理复杂问题的多 Agent 系统。他列出的实施难点包括系统架构、数据管道、MCP 和安全，以及技术部署完成后的工作流程重设计。[S6]

**值得关注：**他据此看好实施服务与前线部署工程师（FDE）的机会。这是对市场需求的判断，而非已经得到订单或收入数据验证的结论。[S6]

## Builder 动态

### datasette-charts 0.4a0：用实验插件检验扩展接口

Simon Willison 于 11 月 27 日记录了 datasette-charts 0.4a0 发布。该插件已有允许其他插件定义新图表类型的 hook；他让 Claude Opus 5.5 构建实验插件来试用接口，发现了一批设计摩擦点，本次版本针对这些问题作出改进。[S13]

配套网站 charts.datasette.io 也已加入插件作者教程，以及核心图表和注释的展示页，每个示例均链接到 Datasette Lite 交互演示。对扩展开发者而言，这次更新的具体价值是接口易用性与学习材料的改善，而非新增模型能力。[S13]

## 值得阅读与观察

- **审视 AI 收入口径。**Nikunj 发帖质疑，部分非算力主营的初创公司把转售算力收入计入年化收入叙事，并将其与低毛利收入、负毛利推理业务混在一起讨论。材料未提供公司名称或财务证据，应视为待核实的行业指控；可提炼的尽调问题是：收入来源、毛利率和持续性是否被分别披露？[S1]
- **能力曲线不等于工作替代时间表。**Dan Shipper 介绍文章时强调，实验室中的能力增长图表不宜直接用于预测人类工作的未来。本次仅提供文章导语，无法据此复述其完整论证或判断证据强弱。[S7]
- **对“竞赛不可避免”的反思。**ryolu_ 的帖子将递归自我改进竞赛描述为预算、研发方向等一连串人为决策，而非不可改变的趋势。这是一篇立场性讨论；所提供文本末尾截断，其中关于失控和滥用的描述属于风险设想，不是已发生事件。[S2]

digests.title: AI 日报：Agent 服务商机会、支付争议与本地推理基准
digests.summary: 本期关注以 Agent 重构服务公司的商业判断、Replit 上的 Gemini 4 体验线索，以及面向 AMD 硬件的 llama.cpp 基准看板；另观察 Agent 支付与 AI 内容同质化讨论。[S1][S5][S12][S13][S14]
digests.content:
## 今日重点

### Agent 的商业机会：重构服务公司，而不只是销售工具

Aaron Levie 提出，以 Agent 为中心新建或改造服务公司，可能成为广告、IT 转型、管理咨询、金融等领域的机会。他认为，深厚的领域知识仍然重要，而 Agent 有望扩大项目交付能力，让服务商争取更多客户、覆盖原本不经济的小客户，或提供过去难以实现的成果。[S1]

**这是一项商业判断，而非已验证的行业结果。** 原文所称交付能力获得“10 倍”放大，没有附带测量依据。值得关注的推论是：竞争优势可能来自“专业知识、客户信任与 Agent 交付流程”的组合，而不只是使用模型本身；既有服务商的客户关系也可能成为转型优势。[S1]

## Builder 动态

### Replit 出现 Gemini 4 体验线索

Amjad Masad 发帖称赞 Gemini 4，并邀请读者到 Replit 体验。该条目提供了产品体验入口的线索，但没有说明具体模型版本、可用范围、价格或评测结果，不能据此认定 Gemini 4 在本期正式发布，也不足以判断其能力提升幅度。[S5]

## 开源趋势

### llama.cpp 面向 AMD 硬件的基准看板

Hugging Face 博客新增条目的标题为《Introducing the llama.cpp benchmark dashboard for AMD Ryzen and Radeon》，主题是面向 AMD Ryzen 与 Radeon 的 llama.cpp 基准看板。[S14]

本次资料只有标题与元数据，没有正文或测试数据。因此可以将其列为本地推理性能评估的关注入口，但尚不能比较具体硬件、模型或推理配置的表现。[S14]

## 值得阅读与观察

- **Agent 支付：有争议的前瞻议题。** swyx 将其视为面向 2028 年的重要方向，并形容讨论立场高度分化。这反映的是作者对趋势与分歧的判断；条目没有提供交易规模、采用率或具体落地案例，不能据此判断市场已经成熟。[S12]
- **AI 内容是否正在抹平个人表达？** Simon Willison 摘引 Jack Despain Zhou 的批评：从视频、会议演讲到邮件，越来越多内容呈现出可辨识的 Claude 式表达。其阅读价值在于提醒创作者审视 AI 辅助写作后的个人声音与署名责任；这属于文化批评和个人观察，而非对内容同质化程度的量化研究。[S13]

digests.title: AI 日报｜11月26日：OpenAI 测试隐私推理，长时编程案例落地
digests.summary: OpenAI 小范围测试 Private Inference，并修正 GPT-6.2 用量折扣错误；Karpathy 展示长时数据编程案例，Gemini 新增66种本地语音与口音选项。[S3][S12][S11][S5]
digests.content:
## 今日重点

### OpenAI 小范围测试 Private Inference
Sam Altman 表示，OpenAI 正与少量客户测试 Private Inference，该产品属于 OpenAI Private Intelligence。他同时称，ZDR 配合 Private Safety Processing，可在不向 OpenAI 人员开放底层内容的情况下进行自动安全审查。[S3]

**值得关注：**隐私保护可能扩大前沿模型可承接的企业工作范围，但当前条目未披露具体技术架构、定价、普遍开放时间或独立验证结果，不能据此推断所有处理环节的隐私边界。[S3]

### GPT-6.2 修正计费错误，同样工作将消耗更多套餐额度
OpenAI 的 Thibault Sottiaux 表示，GPT-6.2 上线时的计费错误，使多数用户的 Astra 和 Sol 用量获得了不正确的折扣，目前已修复。按其披露，相比上周，用户使用 GPT-6.2 Astra 和 Sol 将分别快40%和25%触及额度上限；其他模型不受影响，历史差额不追收。[S12]

官方还将为 Go、Plus、Pro 和 Business 用户各补发一次可留存的额度重置。这里披露的是**套餐额度消耗变化**，并非宣布订阅价格上涨；依赖这两个模型运行固定工作流的用户，需要重新评估额度预算。[S12]

## Builder 动态

### Karpathy 展示约7小时完成的美国数据地图
Karpathy 分享了一个使用 Claude Code 桌面端、Opus 5.5 medium 档并开启 ultracode 构建的项目：将美国公共数据整理成《文明》风格的地图。据其描述，任务耗时约7小时，生成约4.5万行代码，整合31个真实数据源，并统一到25公里六边形网格。[S11]

项目包含19种数据视图、524个都会区的城市视图，以及覆盖3,100多个县的数据探索功能。其意义不只是生成界面，而是展示了模型连续执行数据下载、解析、空间对齐与交互开发的能力。不过，这仍是作者自述的单个案例；作者明确提到遗漏了部分州和地区，不能将其视为完整性或数据准确性已获验证的产品。[S11]

### Gemini 扩充本地语音与口音选项
Josh Woodward 表示，Gemini 新增66种本地语音与口音选项。条目没有列出完整清单、地区可用性或接口支持范围，因此不宜将其解读为新增66种语言。[S5]

### datasette-charts 0.3a0 增加图表标注
Simon Willison 发布的版本说明显示，datasette-charts 0.3a0 支持为图表添加线条、阴影区域和标签，并可通过图表构建界面调整；安装 Datasette Agent 后，也可让智能体生成带标注的图表。对数据分析应用而言，这是把图表生成进一步推进到解释性表达的一项具体更新。[S13]

### Thariq 宣布从 Anthropic 转投 OpenAI
Thariq 在个人帖文中宣布加入 OpenAI，并回顾了在 Anthropic 的经历。条目未披露其新职位、所属团队或具体职责，因此目前只能确认这项本人宣布的人员流动，不能据此判断产品或组织调整。[S8]

## 值得阅读与观察

### 大规模软件迁移：关键条件是结果可验证
Amjad Masad 提出，只要能够验证结果，大规模软件迁移如今已具可行性，并强调其对老化关键基础设施的重要性。这是一项判断，而非条目中已被案例或指标证实的结论；对 Builder 的启发是，评估迁移自动化时，应把验证能力与代码生成能力一起考察。[S7]

### SQLite 远程快照复制：不必先在本地腾出完整副本空间
Simon Willison 介绍，sqlite3_rsync 可通过 SSH 将 SQLite 数据库快照复制到另一台机器，无须先在源机器创建完整本地副本，也支持通过页哈希比较减少重复传输。这对磁盘空间紧张的实例备份尤其有用。[S15]

**时间边界：**这不是新发布的工具。来源说明，其已于2024年10月作为实验功能加入 SQLite 3.47.0，并在2025年5月的3.50.0中增强；本次新增的是介绍文章。[S15]

digests.title: AI 日报｜11月25日：MCP 配套技能与 Agent 工作流演进
digests.summary: MCP 服务可携带技能供 Claude Code 使用；ChatGPT Business 提供限时权益。[S4][S5] 本期还关注多 Agent 实践、历史研究案例及开放模型的全球采用讨论。[S1][S13][S10]
digests.content:
## 今日重点

### MCP 服务可自带技能
Boris Cherny 表示，MCP 服务器现在可以随附自身的 skills，让 Claude Code 开箱即知如何使用这些服务。新增条目未提供配置方式、兼容范围或具体示例。[S4]

### ChatGPT Business 提供限时权益
Thibault Sottiaux 宣布，面向 ChatGPT Business 团队提供一次“banked reset”，以及截至 12 月 31 日不额外收费的 fast mode。原帖未解释重置机制、额度及具体适用条件，不宜据此理解为无限量使用。[S5]

## Builder 动态

- **Antigravity 多 Agent 实践教程**：Peter Yang 分享了一门免费、17 分钟的视频课程，介绍 Gemini 4 Neon 与 Antigravity 的组合。他称 Orchestrator 和 `/swarm` 适合多 Agent 规划与构建，曾同时运行 42 个 Agent；`/grill-me` 可通过追问澄清需求。有关远程控制优于 Claude Code 的说法属于其个人体验，并非独立评测结论。[S1]
- **把编程 Agent 做成可嵌入内核**：Guillermo Rauch 解释，其提及工具采用 CLI，是因为它只是 `libfx` 的薄封装；目标是构建尽可能小且智能的编程 Agent 内核，嵌入浏览器、服务器、移动端和桌面等环境。这是设计目标，条目没有证明这些平台均已得到支持。[S8]
- **OC 的维护重心转向可靠性**：Peter Steinberger 表示，OC 已在专业消费者和企业采用中找到定位，近期主要投入速度、可靠性与安全性，同时提及新记忆系统及即将到来的 OpenClaw ID。他也强调了维护可靠、免费开源软件的工作量与情绪压力。采用情况与功能评价均为作者自述，未附量化数据。[S12]

## 值得阅读

### 历史研究中的“提出线索—档案核验”案例
Simon Willison 转述历史学教授 Mark Humphries 的案例：GPT-6.2 Astra 据称在 22 分钟内，为耶鲁大学 Beinecke 图书馆收藏的一本匿名 1808 年素描册识别作者，并提出一份纸质档案来源作为验证线索；据该案例叙述，后续查验支持了其假设。[S13]

**阅读价值**在于模型不仅给出归属判断，还指向可进一步核查的史料。不过，这仍是单个案例报告，不能据此推断模型处理历史归属问题的普遍准确率；现有摘录也不足以复核完整证据链。[S13]

### 编程 Agent 何时开始真正省时间？
Willison 在《十二个月里的三个 LLM 拐点》中回顾自己的使用变化：他认为，Claude Opus 4.5 让 Claude Code 从需要频繁纠正的工具，变成处理多数日常编程问题时能够带来明确提速的助手。这是个人经验判断，不是统一基准测试。[S14]

所给摘录只展开了文章开头，无法据此完整概括标题中的三个拐点。[S14]

## 观察

- **Token 需求可能随 Agent 工作方式阶梯式增长**：Amjad Masad 提出，从自动补全、聊天到 Agent、长时自主 Agent 和群体协作，每次工具框架创新都会打开更大的潜在消耗空间，但用户找到实际用途存在滞后。这是一种需求增长假说，条目未提供用量或收入数据验证。[S3]
- **开放模型竞争也关乎部署控制权**：Masad 认为，各国对本土基础设施和自主控制的需求，会影响模型、芯片及技术栈的全球采用；开放模型因此具有战略意义。这篇观点帖适合用来观察“前沿能力”之外的竞争维度，但不能当作各国采购趋势已被证实的结论。[S10]

digests.title: AI 日报｜Claude 整合插件生态，GLM-5.4 采用循环 Transformer
digests.summary: Claude 推进插件整合、交付工具与企业安全能力；GLM-5.4 采用循环 Transformer，但据资料尚未开放权重；Datasette 打通对话制图与面板状态联动。[S6][S7][S8][S14][S16]
digests.content:
## 今日重点

### Claude：连接器与技能合并为插件

Claude 官方宣布将 connectors 与 skills 统一为 plugins，用于连接工具、扩展技能，或同时完成两者。插件已面向 Free、Pro、Max、Ultra 套餐开放，Team 与 Enterprise 将随后支持；官方称可浏览的插件超过 10,000 个。这里的数量是官方披露的目录规模，不代表插件质量或使用量。[S8]

企业端另有两项更新：
- **Claude Ship 测试版**：11 月 23 日宣布面向 Team 和 Enterprise 推出。发布者将其定位于改善代码生成之后的 PR 交付环节，但本次材料未披露具体功能、权限边界或效果数据。[S7]
- **零数据保留与安全防护结合**：支持零数据保留（ZDR）的 Enterprise Frontier Safeguards（EFS）面向符合条件的企业进入公开测试。官方称，该机制可跨多次请求识别滥用，同时兼容 ZDR，并与超过 100 家客户共同开发；具体实现方式未在所给材料中展开。[S6]

### GLM-5.4：以循环层增加计算深度

据 Simon Willison 的介绍，Z.ai 的 GLM-5.4 已可使用，是该实验室首个采用循环 Transformer 架构的模型：让一组共享权重的层迭代运行，以不增加参数量的方式加深计算。**这说明了架构思路，并不直接证明性能优于其他模型**；本次材料没有提供可比较的评测结果。[S14]

接入方面，作者测试时需订阅 Coding Plan，普通 API 暂不能访问该模型；Coding Plan 密钥可通过 OpenAI 兼容的 Responses API 使用。文章同时指出，GLM-5.4 当时尚未开放权重，因此不宜将其归为开源模型发布。[S14]

## Builder 动态

### Datasette：对话生成图表，并跟随用户操作更新上下文

11 月 24 日发布的 **datasette-charts 0.2a0** 接入 Datasette Agent：用户可在聊天中指定数据表并要求制图，图表既能内嵌展示，也能在侧边面板的图表构建器中打开。演示中，用户在面板切换数据后，Agent 能在后续问答中识别并解释新的图表内容。[S16]

配套的 **datasette-agent 0.7a1** 改进了 iframe 侧边面板的 URL 片段导航，以便与通过 fragment hash 表达交互状态的插件更深入地集成，并修复图表插件相关问题。这组更新的看点不只是“聊天生成图表”，而是对话与可视化界面之间的状态衔接。[S15][S16]

### OpenAI 内部使用 dots 构建 dots

OpenAI 的 Thibault Sottiaux 表示，dots 正迅速成为内部完成工作的主要方式之一，且已有 dots 参与构建 dots 系统本身。这是一则内部使用情况的陈述；材料没有解释其完整产品形态、开放范围，也没有量化生产力收益。[S5]

## 观察

### 个性化模型评估值得借鉴，但不能外推为通用排名

Guillermo Rauch 称，他让 Fable 分析自己的编程会话，在 Opus 与 Gemini Neon 之间做选择，结果选中了 Neon。这提供了一个实用思路：以个人真实工作记录作为选型依据。但材料未给出评分标准、样本范围或复现实验，因此结果只能视为其个人工作流下的评估，不能据此判定模型整体优劣。[S2]

### ChatGPT 质量提升仍需等待实际验证

Sottiaux 预告，相关更新逐步推送后，用户应能感到 ChatGPT 回答质量显著提升，并提及简化应用、提速及融合聊天与工作的投入。这属于产品方向与效果预期；本次材料没有给出具体模型版本、完整上线时间或评测数据，不宜写成已向所有用户兑现的改进。[S9]

digests.content:
## 今日重点

### AutoClip：从长视频到短视频发布素材

AutoClip 是一款开源 AI 视频剪辑桌面工具。项目介绍称，输入链接后，可将播客、访谈、课程等长视频自动剪成短视频，并生成字幕、封面和发布文案，面向抖音、小红书、TikTok、Reels 与 YouTube Shorts 等平台。[S4]

值得关注的是，它的功能范围不止剪辑，还覆盖内容再利用与发布素材准备。不过，现有资料仅为项目简介，无法确认剪辑质量、平台适配效果或实际使用成本。[S4]

## Builder 动态

### OpenSRE：面向 CI/CD 可靠性的开源 Agent

OpenSRE 将自身定位为服务于 CI/CD 可靠性的开源 Agent。新增资料未说明其具体任务、集成方式或自主执行边界，因此目前适合作为工程自动化方向的观察项目，尚不足以判断落地能力。[S1]

## 值得阅读

### 用 Claude 构建 HTML 下拉框样式对照页

Simon Willison 在 11 月 22 日的文章中记录：由于不满意 HTML `<select>` 在不同浏览器中的默认外观，他让 Claude Fable 5.2 制作展示多种样式方案的页面，并计划在桌面与移动浏览器中截图比较。[S5]

经过实验，他偏好的方案使用 `appearance: none` 移除原生外观，再配置边框、内边距与 SVG 背景箭头。这提供了一个具体的 AI 辅助前端工作流：先生成可比较的样例，再通过浏览器检查选择方案；不能据此认定所有浏览器的兼容性已获验证。[S5]

## 观察

本次新增项目中，AutoClip 指向内容生产自动化，OpenSRE 指向工程可靠性自动化，体现了两种不同的 Agent／AI 工具应用方向；仅凭这两条简介，不能推断行业整体趋势。[S1][S4]

上述两个 GitHub 项目均未提供发布时间，本期仅作新增收录，不将其表述为今日创建或发布。[S1][S4]

digests.title: AI 日报｜黎曼猜想证明声明待核验，Agent 工具链持续细化
digests.summary: 黎曼猜想相关证明声明引发人机协作讨论，但所给材料未证明其获独立确认；ChatGPT/Codex 桌面端继续迭代，Agent 技能与插件工具增多，Token 滥用暴露产品成本风险。[S28][S11][S13][S17][S26]
digests.content:
## 今日重点

### 黎曼猜想相关声明引发关注，不能等同于已确认突破
- **当事人声明**：Simon Willison 摘引 Levent Alpöge 的文字称，后者相信自己与 Claude 找到了黎曼猜想的证明，方法还可扩展至广义黎曼猜想，并称已完成不依赖额外假设的形式化论证。这是被转引的自述，不是材料所能独立确认的数学结论。[S28]
- **另一条研究线索**：Ravi Vakil 的引文介绍，Alessandro Masullo 也有广义黎曼猜想的候选证明，Brian Conrad 已持续审阅数月并提供反馈；该工作被明确描述为未使用 AI。引文仍将其称为候选证明，而非已获最终确认的成果。[S29]
- **编辑判断**：讨论应区分“提出证明”“形式化声明”与“获得独立核验”。现有材料不足以确认上述证明成立，也不足以判断两项工作的关系。社交平台已出现将其称为“突破”的评论，报道不宜直接沿用这一确定性表述。[S7][S28][S29]

### Token 滥用正在影响 AI 产品的试用策略
据 Simon Willison 对 Claire Vo 视频的介绍，ChatPRD 遭遇反复注册免费试用、套用促销码，以及借其 Agent 获取算力或开展其他商业活动的滥用；Claire 正逐步取消免费试用。对 Builder 而言，这个案例提示：试用额度不仅是获客成本，也可能成为被转售或挪用的资源。材料未提供损失规模。[S26]

## Builder 动态

- **ChatGPT/Codex 桌面端继续迭代**：11 月 22 日的帖子称，团队已在准备下一次较大更新，并就前一天的桌面应用更新征集反馈。现有信息没有列出已上线功能或下一版发布时间，不宜据此扩写更新清单。[S11]
- **Muru：AI 辅助开发 Python 应用服务器**：据介绍，mod_wsgi 发起者 Graham Dumpleton 正使用 AI 辅助构建 Rust 服务器 Muru，目标是支持 ASGI、WSGI 应用的开发与生产运行。他持续公开架构和开发过程，涉及 worker、发布、容器、扩缩容及追踪等主题；材料未提供性能对比或成熟度验证。[S30]
- **Amuse 宣布开源**：Amjad Masad 发帖称，由 Replit Missions 构建的 Amuse 已开源。所给文本没有项目功能、许可证或部署方式，暂只能确认这项开源声明。[S9]

## 开源趋势

以下依据仓库简介整理；所给材料没有 Star 增量、下载量或使用数据，因此不能据此判断热度排名。

| 方向 | 项目与具体看点 |
| --- | --- |
| 安全技能 | **Claude-BugHunter**：简介列出 82 项技能、15 个斜杠命令，以及覆盖 24 类核心漏洞的 681 个已披露报告模式，面向漏洞挖掘与外部红队工作。[S13] |
| 开发方法与扩展 | **superpowers** 自述为 Agent 技能框架与软件开发方法；**cursor/plugins** 提供 Cursor 插件规范及官方插件。[S14][S17] |
| 软件接口 Agent 化 | **CLI-Anything** 以让软件具备面向 Agent 的命令行接口为目标；这是项目定位，不能理解为已适配所有软件。[S15] |
| 跨工具技能 | **stitch-skills** 面向 Stitch MCP server，简介称遵循 Agent Skills 开放标准，适配多种编码 Agent。[S23] |
| 数据接入 | **Firecrawl** 将搜索、抓取和数据访问整合到一个 API，简介称可访问 550 多个数据提供方；实际覆盖与服务条件未在材料中展开。[S18] |
| 垂直工作流 | **diagram-design** 提供 45 类图表的 HTML、SVG 设计能力；**app-store-compliance** 将商店拒审模式、隐私检查和提交前检查整理为手册与 Agent 技能。[S21][S24] |

**趋势判断**：这批项目的共同方向，是把开发方法、工具接口和领域检查项封装成 Agent 可调用的组件，而不只是发布独立聊天产品。这是对本批样本的归纳，不代表整个开源生态的统计结论。[S13][S14][S15][S23][S24]

## 值得阅读

1. **Muru 开发记录：经验如何参与 AI 编程。** 摘录强调，即使 AI 承担大量表层工作，判断“哪里还不够好”仍依赖开发者积累。适合关注 AI 辅助工程实践、而非只看生成速度的读者。[S30]
2. **PostgreSQL 19 的 `WAIT FOR LSN`。** 11 月 19 日的文章介绍，通过等待备库回放到指定日志位置，让后续查询读到此前在主库完成的写入；还说明了可选超时的行为。这是早于本期主要动态的工程阅读补充。[S25]
3. **llm-gemini 0.38.1：推理档位与成本。** 作者称此次修复补上部分模型的 `xhigh` 设置；其示例中，同一模型从 `high` 切换至 `xhigh` 后，输出 Token 从 5,311 增至 31,477，费用从 3.99 美分增至 23.61 美分。这只是单个示例，不足以证明更高档位对所有任务都更划算。[S27]

## 观察

- **人机协作能力仍值得单独评估。** trq212 的连续帖子认为，与模型合作推动前沿本身就是技术能力，并表示尚未看到这项能力的收益递减。这是作者观点；它与 Muru 开发记录中强调人的质量判断相呼应，但不能替代生产率实测。[S4][S5][S6][S30]
- **多 Agent 协作出现可跟踪的组织线索。** Amjad Masad 转述一名高中生尝试让 GTA6 在 PC 上运行，并强调通过 GitHub Issues 协调 Agent 群。值得继续观察的是任务拆分与验收机制；材料没有代码、演示或独立验证，不能确认移植进度与效果。[S12]
- **供应商数据回传疑问尚缺证据。** swyx 发帖质疑某些提供方是否在秘密回传数据，但文本没有指明提供方、回传内容或技术证据。目前只能记录为待核实质疑，不能据此认定存在隐私违规。[S1]

items.excerpt:
The greatest tragedy right now in Silicon Valley that NO one wants to talk about is how some startups are "reselling" compute and calling it revenue.. not inference, just straight up selling compute to other companies. And, no their primary business is NOT selling compute. 

In this era, where everyone wants to show high "annualized run rate" growth as that's the story that gets marked up, companies are now being even more creative in how to lump "revenue" into a month.

It started with GMV-like revenue with low margins, then inference at negative gross margins and now straight up reselling compute. All lumped into a tidy "ARR". 

Naive investors will lap it up since it allows them to pass deals through IC, and seed investors will celebrate their markups - but zero shot this ends well.

items.title: the race is not inevitable
items.excerpt:
the race is not inevitable

last year was fun.

the models weren't that good yet, so i had to care about every detail. i pushed each thing until it had my thoughts and my designs. the tool helped. i did the driving.

now the roles have flipped. we describe and watch things come back finished. we used to drive our dreams. more and more, we just watch.

we set out to make things that give us more freedom. now we're racing toward something we might not be able to control.

recursive self-improvement. intelligence building more intelligence, until we're no longer the ones who understand what's happening.

that's the end game. the point where nobody is driving.

the big labs are racing to get there first. the same system that cures a disease could design a new virus, or find every hole in the internet all at once. only the selected few with access could do anything about it.

and somehow the possibility of losing everything we love becomes an argument for going faster.

because someone else might get there first, and they might be less careful.
because the company needs to survive.
because too much money is already committed.

everyone has a good reason to keep going toward an outcome nobody wants. so we call it inevitable. then nobody has to answer for it.

but a race is made of decisions. someone approves the budget. someone decides the next model will help build the one after it.

and we practice living inside the race long before we build it at the scale of civilization.

sleep becomes recovery for work. friendship becomes a network. curiosity has to become a project before we let ourselves spend time on it.

we get very rational. we start acting like the machines we're building.

even our feelings have to defend themselves.

items.excerpt:
This is the diffusion challenge and opportunity in a nutshell. Most people will probably get stuck with the use-cases that initially wowed them with AI, and have little incentive to move onto the next thing that will unlock another level of productivity.

Even a large number of organizations can get stuck by being “satisfied” with AI gains, well before having full blown agents that can do any amount of work in the background or agent swarms that can take on complex, ambiguous problems.

Much of this comes down to the technical complexity of implementing the architectures around this. Despite lots of effort to simplify the UXes, there’s still a lot of system work, data pipelines, MCPs, and security that needs to be worked through to get the most out of agents. But even when you’re done with that, you still need to redesign your workflow or process overall to get the full benefits from agents.

This is why there’s so much opportunity to be an organization that figures this out early. It’s also why there’s going to be massive services and FDE opportunities right now as well, since most companies can’t do this on their own.

Huge opportunity right now to build new services firms from the ground up, or transform existing ones, with agents at the center. 

The expertise that services firms in theory should have is as important as ever because you still need deep domain understanding to get the most out of agents. But now the ability to deliver on projects has a 10X multiplier. This means that you can make clients happier, compete to win more of them, go after smaller customers not in the TAM before, or deliver outcomes that weren’t really conceivable.

This is going to happen in advertising, IT transformation, management consulting, finance, and a number of other fields that historically are just fully constrained by the speed of their workforce for output. 

This is a huge opportunity right now for those starting these firms. I wouldn’t count out existing players that commit to the transformation either as existing customer trust goes a long way. But they have to move quickly to make it work.

items.title: 12 tips for people who posted on LinkedIn but now wanna post on X
items.excerpt:
12 tips for people who posted on LinkedIn but now wanna post on X

A lot of people I know are moving their posting from LinkedIn to X. When they ask me how I grew 80k followers on X in one year, here’s what I tell them:

1. LinkedIn is a stage. X is a party. First you find your crowd, then you listen to what they're already talking about. Don't start talking until you get it

2. You can't reach the C-suite directly. LinkedIn is a professional network, so you can go straight to decision makers. X doesn't work like that. You have to get mass attention first, and then the right people notice you

3. Post way more than you think. On LinkedIn, 3-5 posts a week counts as a lot. I posted 3 times a day on X for 6 months. Some founders I follow post 5 times a day. It's not that they're on X all day. They just don't overthink it

4. Make posting a reflex. If you spend too long on a post, you won't post. Whenever a thought comes up, post it right there. No planning, no scheduling, no waiting for the right time

5. It's a numbers game. Most posts won't do well. Maybe 1 in 10 will. Maybe 1 in 50 goes viral. That's normal

6. Half your posts should be reactions. LinkedIn is mostly “proactive content”. On X, at least at the start, half of what you post should be “reactive content”: replies, quote tweets, commentary on what others already said

7. Know the difference between a reply and a quote tweet. A reply is like a LinkedIn DM. It says "notice me." A quote tweet uses someone else's content to grow your own account

8. Fix your feed first. If you wanna talk about cybersecurity and your feed is all politics, you can't join the right conversations. Pick a few big names in your niche. See who they follow and who they engage with, and follow those people too. Like, bookmark and comment.

items.title: sqlite3_rsync: Database Remote-Copy Tool For SQLite
items.excerpt: sqlite3_rsync: Database Remote-Copy Tool For SQLite This additional SQLite tool has been around for a while now - it was added as "experimental" in SQLite 3.47.0 in October 2024 and enhanced in SQLite 3.50.0 in May 2025 . It was only today that I understood one of its most attractive characteristics. Normally, if you want to grab a snapshot copy of a SQLite database, you need to use either the backup API or VACUUM INTO . In both cases you need enough disk space to create a duplicate copy of your database, so if you're on a small instance and you already use more than half of the available disk you are plain out of luck. sqlite3_rsync can copy a snapshot of your database over an SSH connection to another machine, without first needing to create a full local copy! It's also good for synchronizing an existing copy of a database without re-transmitting the entire thing over the network. It works in a similar way to regular rsync: The core idea behind the protocol is that the replica sends cryptographic hashes for pages or groups of pages over to the origin side. The origin sends back page content that differs, or requests finer-grain hashes if a multi-page hash does not match. If the origin and replica start out being vastly different, the total network bandwidth can exceed the size of the entire database, due to the overhead of exchanging hashes, but the excess bandwidth is not great - a few percent at most. items.excerpt:
America can build the best frontier models and still lose the global AI race. Which is why Jensen’s return matters far beyond Nvidia.

Governments around the world want sovereign AI: models they can run on their own soil, on their own infrastructure, under their own control.

If American companies won’t meet that demand, Chinese companies will. Countries will start with Chinese models, then adopt Chinese infrastructure and chips. Having the smartest model won’t mean much if most of the world runs on someone else’s stack.

We’ve seen a version of this play out with Huawei. China understood that supplying the world’s telecom infrastructure creates lasting strategic influence. Once a country builds its networks around your equipment, it also builds technical expertise, supplier relationships, and future investment around it. Replacing that equipment becomes expensive and disruptive (the US government is now trying to finance replacement operations but it’s been difficult).

That’s why Jensen’s backing of the American open-model ecosystem is so important. Open models give startups the freedom to compete and give countries a reason to build on American technology.

We need both frontier leadership and global adoption. Open models are essential to getting both. https://t.co/f34FKKbljl

Ladybird is an astonishingly ambitious project: a new browser, in 2026, with its own implementation of most of the key components - HTML parsing, CSS engine, layout, JavaScript, even WebAssembly. It still uses a few external components - things like HarfBuzz for text shaping, Skia for 2D graphics, ffmpeg for video, and SQLite for the things you do with SQLite. Everything else is part of Ladybird, or code brought in from Ladybird's even more ambitious predecessor project SerenityOS . This morning the Ladybird project released their first alpha , which means you can now install the browser (on macOS or Linux) without having to compile it yourself! I've been trying it out today, and it's very impressive. It feels fast, the UI is lightweight and intuitive, and most of the websites I've tried to load in it have worked as they should. items.title: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer
items.excerpt: GLM-5.4: Toward Generalized Coding with Our First Loop Transformer GLM 5.4 is now available from Chinese AI lab Z.ai. It's their first model to use a looped transformer architecture, which they describe like this: In a standard Transformer, each layer runs once per forward pass. In a Loop Transformer, a group of weight-shared layers runs for multiple iterations, refining the hidden states from the previous pass. This gives us a deeper network without increasing the parameter count. This is the second mention of looped transformers I've seen in the past week - the first was Inkling 2 Mini from Thinking Machines Lab on November 20th, who said: Inkling 2 Mini is a looped transformer, running the middle layers of the model three times for every token. This allows the model to apply more reasoning and reach the right answer with fewer tokens, especially on tasks such as agentic coding that depend on reasoning quality. GLM 5.4 is not (yet?) available as open weights. I tried it out using the Z.ai API, for which I had to sign up for their Coding Plan subscription because 5.4 cannot currently be accessed through the regular API. It turns out both coding plan and regular API share the same OpenAI-compatible Responses API (at https://api.z.ai/api/v1 ), and the API key for the coding plan worked with that and gave me access to the new model. I built a llm-glm plugin , then realized that llm-zai by Tommy Hughes already exists! items.excerpt:
This post nails why we why we should take the Riemann Hypothesis breakthrough very seriously, even beyond math. We’re entering an era where solving problems will look very different from how we solved them in the past.

“This is not theory-building in the usual sense. It is something much weirder and more alien. The best human mathematicians know how to build theory, painstakingly, to reach a goal. But no human brain, on its own, is capable of creating a wormhole that requires a 25,000 page long tour through existing infrastructure with no obvious or realistic connection to the goal. But huge credit to Levent here: I think no current AI, on its own, is capable of this either.”

It used to be the case that to solve a particular problem - code, life sciences, math, cyber, engineering, and so on - you were ultimately bound by how much information an individual or team could retain and understand about the space. More information or more team members don’t always help, because it gets harder to connect the dots or coordinate amongst everyone. AI changes that completely. 

For the first time ever we can decouple the human context limits and ability to work through information from our ability to drive productivity or discoveries. This is likely not just a small increase in the kinds of discoveries we can drive, but a qualitative shift in human output.

items.title: Token fraud is here and it’s BAD (YouTube)
items.excerpt: Token fraud is here and it’s BAD (YouTube) Claire Vo runs ChatPRD , an AI platform that helps product managers "turn an idea into a spec". The product has been live since the GPT-4 era, and Claire has been building it in public for much of that time. In this YouTube video (see also the accompanying Twitter post ) Claire describes the flood of token fraud she has seen from groups abusing the product's free trial, sometimes just to get free AI usage but often to resell tokens or run other commercial enterprises on top of the ChatPRD agent. I am funding a international Roblox and Fortnite map studio. They run a loop of free trials and promo codes and then tunnel to my agent and use it to build Roblox and Fortnite maps. Apparently one of the common prompts Claire saw running through her agent involved SVGs of pelicans riding bicycles! Presumably the token scammers are using that to help sniff the underlying models - different model families have a definite signature, and I've used it like this in the past to try and guess the identity of stealth preview models on platforms like OpenRouter. Claire is winding down her free trials entirely, which sadly looks like the right decision in the face of this abuse. Tags: youtube , ai , generative-ai , llms , pelican-riding-a-bicycle , ai-misuse

items.title: Muru
items.excerpt: Muru Graham Dumpleton started mod_wsgi 20 years ago, and has been thinking about the ideal way to serve Python web applications in production ever since. Muru is his new, AI-assisted Rust server that aims to provide the best possible tools for running ASGI and WSGI Python apps both in development and production. As he did with wrapture , he's been publishing an extraordinarily detailed account of the project as he works on it - as part of his development process. Here's everything he's published so far, all in the last three weeks: 2026-11-04 — Twenty years of mod_wsgi, and what comes next 2026-11-05 — A first look at Muru 2026-11-07 — Muru: looking inside the workers 2026-11-08 — Muru: how it fits together 2026-11-09 — Muru: import once, fork many 2026-11-10 — Muru: HTTPS in development 2026-11-11 — Muru: WSGI and ASGI together 2026-11-11 — AI as a lifestyle choice 2026-11-12 — Muru: releases, not restarts 2026-11-13 — Muru: canaries without a service mesh 2026-11-14 — Muru: a better tenant in a container 2026-11-15 — Muru: working with Kubernetes, not around it 2026-11-16 — Muru: scaling from what the workers report 2026-11-17 — Muru: scaling to zero 2026-11-18 — Muru: overlays on a schedule 2026-11-19 — Muru: noticing and responding 2026-11-20 — Muru: a toolbar on every page 2026-11-21 — Muru: tracing in the toolbar 2026-11-22 — Muru: when lazy imports help That post about AI as a lifestyle choice is particularly worth a read: The AI may be doing a lot of the work on the surface, but deciding what isn't good enough yet is still down to me, and twenty years of getting things wrong with mod_wsgi turns out to be useful for that. I am prepared to put in the hard work to keep polishing Muru until it is something I would trust, and something you would too. Tags: graham-dum
